title: The fish plush is gone
opening: {cat} had exactly one fish plush. Now {cat} has none. Nobody saw anything, and {cat} is not talking. Look around the room, each of you. You won't see the same things.

beats.title: The empty basket

halves.text: The basket by the sofa is empty. In the cushion there's a dent shaped exactly like a fish.
Small paw prints leave the basket and head for the window. They are very sure of themselves.

beats.together: The plush went toward the window. Nobody carries a plush to a window by accident.

beats.title: The windowsill

halves.text: One black feather on the sill. Glossy, smug, and much too big for a sparrow.
Three thin scratches on the outside of the glass, as if someone knocked with a very small, very rude knuckle.

beats.together: A big black bird has been at this window, and not for the first time.

beats.title: The torn letter

halves.text: Under the rug, the top half of a letter: "Dear {cat}, I have the shi…"
In a fold of the curtain, the bottom half: "…ny thing you wanted. Dusk, at the sill. Bring the fish."

beats.together: "Dear {cat}, I have the shiny thing you wanted. Dusk, at the sill. Bring the fish." So {cat} wasn't robbed. {cat} was invited.

beats.title: The stash

halves.text: Behind the armchair, a tidy heap: a bottle cap, a scrap of foil, one earring. Somebody has been collecting.
The heap has a sign made of lint. It points at the sill. Under it, a tiny drawing of a fish. It's good, actually.

beats.together: {cat} has been saving shiny things for a deal. The fish was the big offer.

beats.title: Dusk

halves.text: At dusk the window goes dark in the shape of a bird. It tilts its head. It looks at {cat}. {cat} looks at the ceiling.
On the sill, something small and round catches the last of the light. It wasn't there this morning.

beats.together: The visitor came at dusk, as written. And {cat} ended up with something round and shiny.

ask: Who has the fish plush now?

suspects.name: The vacuum
suspects.blurb: Loud, greedy, lives in a cupboard. Has never once been to the windowsill.

suspects.name: The crow
suspects.blurb: Black feathers, shiny habits, writes letters. Very sure of itself.

suspects.name: The draft
suspects.blurb: Gets blamed for everything. Has never been seen holding anything.

ending.title: A fair trade
lines: The crow lands on the sill at dusk, right on time.
{cat} carries the fish plush over with great ceremony.
The crow looks at the plush. The crow looks at {cat}. The crow, who has never been generous, lets a round shiny button drop.
{cat} has what {cat} wanted. The crow has a fish. Nobody is sorry.
The crow now knows exactly where you live. It will be back.

verdicts.both: You both said the crow. Case closed.
verdicts.one: One of you said the crow and one didn't. Comparing notes is most of the game.
verdicts.none: Not the crow, this time. The crow doesn't mind, and neither does {cat}.

souvenir.name: The shiny button
souvenir.note: Traded fair and square. It lives on your board now.
